# chans

```go
import "carswell.tech/x/chans"
```

Package chans provides small helpers for working with Go channels: bridging them to and from the stdlib's [iter.Seq](<https://pkg.go.dev/iter/#Seq>) iterators, and splitting a bidirectional channel \(or minting a fresh one\) into separate send\-only and receive\-only views.

[Iter2Chan](<#Iter2Chan>) and [Chan2Iter](<#Chan2Iter>) convert between iter.Seq\[T\] and \<\-chan T / chan T in each direction. [Pair](<#Pair>) and [Split](<#Split>) both return a \(chan\<\- T, \<\-chan T\) pair backed by the same underlying channel — Pair makes a new channel of the given buffer length, Split takes an existing one — so an action on one view \(a send, or closing the send side\) is observable through the other.

## Index

- [func Chan2Iter\[T any\]\(c \<\-chan T\) iter.Seq\[T\]](<#Chan2Iter>)
- [func Iter2Chan\[T any\]\(seq iter.Seq\[T\]\) \<\-chan T](<#Iter2Chan>)
- [func Pair\[T any\]\(buflen int\) \(chan\<\- T, \<\-chan T\)](<#Pair>)
- [func Split\[T any\]\(c chan T\) \(chan\<\- T, \<\-chan T\)](<#Split>)


<a name="Chan2Iter"></a>
## func [Chan2Iter](<https://github.com/dccarswell/go/blob/main/x/chans/iter.go#L24>)

```go
func Chan2Iter[T any](c <-chan T) iter.Seq[T]
```

Chan2Iter returns an iter.Seq\[T\] that yields the values received from c, in the order they arrive, until c is closed. If the consumer stops ranging over the returned sequence early, no further values are received from c.

<a name="Iter2Chan"></a>
## func [Iter2Chan](<https://github.com/dccarswell/go/blob/main/x/chans/iter.go#L9>)

```go
func Iter2Chan[T any](seq iter.Seq[T]) <-chan T
```

Iter2Chan drains seq onto a new unbuffered channel from a background goroutine, closing the channel once seq is exhausted. The goroutine sends are paced by the channel: if the caller stops reading before the channel is closed, the goroutine blocks on its next send indefinitely.

<a name="Pair"></a>
## func [Pair](<https://github.com/dccarswell/go/blob/main/x/chans/pair.go#L7>)

```go
func Pair[T any](buflen int) (chan<- T, <-chan T)
```

Pair creates a new channel with the given buffer length and returns send\-only and receive\-only views of it. Both views share the same underlying channel: a value sent on the first is received on the second, and closing the first is observable as a closed channel on the second.

<a name="Split"></a>
## func [Split](<https://github.com/dccarswell/go/blob/main/x/chans/split.go#L9>)

```go
func Split[T any](c chan T) (chan<- T, <-chan T)
```

Split returns send\-only and receive\-only views of the existing channel c. Both views share the same underlying channel: a value sent on the first is received on the second, and closing the first is observable as a closed channel on the second. Unlike [Pair](<#Pair>), Split does not create a channel — it only narrows the direction of one you already have, including any values already buffered in it.
